subject: VPC/on-prem IaC interface contracts — review request
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-corp.com>
Cc: infra-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: 2027-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: VPC/on-prem IaC interface contracts — review request

Team / Acme,

Attaching a proposed "interface contracts" doc that spells out the boundaries between Terraform (network + infra), Helm (k8s manifests / service plumbing), and Ansible (on-host bootstrap) for the private VPC/on‑prem deployment pattern we demoed last week. This is meant to be minimal but explicit to avoid overlap during handoff to Acme's ops team.

High level asks: 
- Please review module inputs/outputs in section 2 and call out any missing security knobs (vault/KMS, state encryption, RBAC scoping).
- Confirm that the network segmentation suggested (management, workload, egress) maps to Acme's compliance needs.
- CI/CD: check the proposed pipeline job (ci-job-1423) and the gating steps we list.

Attachments: iac-interfaces-spec.md, terraform-module-matrix.csv. CI job run: https://app.redwood.com/runs/ci-job-1423

Proposed follow-up: 30 min sync Fri 05/14 3pm PT to capture blockers and owners.

Thanks,
Aditya
Aditya Rao
Product Manager, Private Deployments
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Alice Chen <alice.chen@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2027-05-14T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC/on-prem IaC interface contracts — review request

Thanks Aditya — skimmed the spec and a few quick notes before the sync: 

- Inputs/outputs: the terraform module matrix is useful, but we need a canonical "network handle" (string ID) that both TF and Helm reference for DNS and CNI configuration. Today the spec exposes subnet IDs and CIDR blocks; propose adding a single network_token value.
- State storage: if Acme will keep TF state in their S3/GCS equivalent, we need explicit locking instructions (consul/s3-lock). Add a sentence about retention and drift detection frequency.
- Ansible/Bootstrap: call out the exact user account and sudo policy that the playbooks will create. Right now it's implicit.

Also dropping two small CI items: 
1) Gate deployments on `integration-tests/privstack` passing — currently the job filter is `integration-tests/*` and will not stop a partial run.
2) Add a post-deploy smoke test that hits the metadata endpoint from inside the management subnet.

Looking forward to the sync.

-Lauren
Senior PM, Deployment Experience
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: VPC/on-prem IaC interface contracts — review request

Adding some technical constraints that must be decided before we freeze the modules: 

1) Remote state locking: Acme prefers their internal object store, which doesn't support Dynamo-style locks. We should add a lock adapter option in the TF backend to support Consul or Vault-based locks. If they pick Consul, we need a small bootstrap step (ansible) to provision the lock ACLs prior to terraform apply.

2) KMS / envelope encryption: For on‑prem hardware where HSM is not available, we should default to customer KMS in their cloud account. The module should allow three modes: `managed`, `bring-your-own-kms`, `hsm`. Document the minimum key policy (rotate_every = 365d, admins list).

3) DNS override: Helm charts currently assume cluster-local CoreDNS can resolve `private.redwood.internal`. For Acme's network that funnels egress through a transit gateway, we need a documented override (configmap + nodeHosts) to ensure service discovery for the management plane.

4) CI credentials: CI job logs showed one failing step (ci-job-1423) where the terraform plan used overly-broad service account scopes. We need a dedicated low-priv SA per environment.

I'll enumerate these as action items in the doc and mark owners.

-Markus
Director, Infra Engineering
Redwood Inference

Date: 2027-05-14T16:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: VPC/on-prem IaC interface contracts — review request

Thanks for sending this over — we're aligned on most items. A few notes from Acme ops: 

- State & locking: we'll run an internal Consul cluster for locking. Ops has agreed to a small Ansible playbook to provision ACL tokens; can share the playbook template by EOD.
- KMS: we will provide a customer-managed KMS key in our cloud project. We need the TF modules to accept an ARN and not attempt to create keys by default.
- Network segmentation: compliance wants the management plane to be logically separate and only reachable from Acme VPN + Redwood SRE CIDR (two IP ranges). Can you add that in the spec?

Procurement/contracting note: we are ready to sign the network addendum; I'll route the DocuSign link to our legal.

-Alice
Cloud Infrastructure Lead
Acme Analytics

- Add Consul lock adapter and bootstrap playbook stub — Markus (owner: markus_klein) + Mina for Ansible snippets — due 2027-05-18
- TF modules accept KMS ARN — Mina (owner: mina_haddad) — due 2027-05-17
- Tighten CI job filter and add smoke test gate (ci-job-1423) — Aditya (owner: aditya_rao) — due 2027-05-16

Thanks all — appreciate the quick turn on this.

-Aditya
